_provenance: Captured from a real tenant on 2026-10-15 through pm-ai's own Graph client: the first page of GET /chats/{chat}/messages as GraphClient.chat_messages builds it ($top=50, $orderby=lastModifiedDateTime desc, $filter=lastModifiedDateTime gt fourteen days before the capture) for the first listed chat with a message in that window, a meeting chat. Graph accepted the filtered, sorted request, and the rows arrived newest modification first. Redacted before it left the machine. Ids come from HMAC-SHA256 under a random 32-byte key that was never written down, so the mapping cannot be reproduced, or confirmed by hashing a guessed real value: GUIDs come out v4-shaped, Teams ids keep their shape (`19:...@thread.tacv2`, `19:meeting_...@thread.v2`, `..._...@unq.gbl.spaces`), and online-meeting and other opaque ids keep their length and alphabet. People are mapped per user id: one id is one 'Person N' across the channel and chat fixtures, and `mentionText` and the text inside `<at>` carry the same label. Free text: every word is replaced by lowercase letters of random length (2 to 9) in its own script, digits become 0, and punctuation, spacing and HTML entities are kept. Kept as recorded: keys, value types, timestamps (the real instants), Graph enumerations (keys ending in Type or Status, `@odata.type`, `contentType`, `messageType` and the like), the JSON keys inside card attachments, HTML tag names and structural attributes. `href` and `src` become https://example.invalid/<token>; URL fields become https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/redacted/<token>, keeping `?$skiptoken=` where the original had one. Kept whole: all 20 rows. No `GET /chats/{chat}` answer was captured, so there is no `chat` object beside the page. Observed on this page: call started, ended, recording and transcript events are typed `unknownFutureValue`, with the body `<systemEventMessage/>`, an `eventDetail` and no `from`.
